newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian farmers await rains for good oilseeds crop.
newsitem.headline: Indian farmers await rains for good oilseeds crop.

text.p: Indian farmers are banking on a fresh spell of rains considered crucial for a good oilseeds crop, industry officials and analysts said on Thursday.
They said monsoon rains in the end of August or early September would boost the oilseeds crop in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat and states of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
"Farmers are looking forward to the rains for good prospects for the oilseeds crop," said Navinbhai Shah, president of the Bombay Oilseeds and Oil Exchange Ltd.
"Otherwise we will have to revise our production forecast," Shah said.
Analysts said the June-September monsoon rains have been satisfactory so far except in southern Andhra Pradesh state which contiributes about one third of the country's oilseeds output.
"It is a normal and satisfactory situation. One more round of rainfall is required by the end of the month," said a Bombay-based commodity analyst.

Shah said rains in the last week of August would mean India would be able to harvest a summer oilseeds crop of 11 million tonnes, the same as last year, including about 5.7 million tonnes of groundnut in shell.
"But if the rains do not come the oilseeds crop will suffer heavily," Shah said. "This moisture will be required."
He said while Saurashtra region had excellent rains so far oilseeds production in Andhra Pradesh would be hit due to paucity of rains.
"The picture is not good in Andhra Pradesh," Shah said.
But analysts said good rains in other oilseeds growing regions would make up for the shortfall in Andhra Pradesh.
"The loss in Andhra Pradesh could be more than made up in Gujarat," said another commodity analyst.
Shah said domestic edible oil prices were steady on regular import arrivals of palm olein and sunflower oils.
"Domestic arrivals are poor due to lean season but prices are steady on imports," said Shah.
Traders said palm olein prices were steady after touching a low after higher palm olein crop expectations in Malaysia.
They said palm olein was quoted at 26,000 rupees per tonne, marginally up from 25,700 rupees a week ago. Groundnut oil was quoted at 38,000 rupees per tonne against 37,800 rupees last week.
Traders said importers had not made any fresh deals as they had booked commitments up to September and were assessing the size of the new crop due from November.

Trade officials said between November and July, India imported about 140,000 tonnes of palm olein and sunflower oil every month. Between August and October the monthly imports would rise to about 180,000 tonnes due to Hindu festivals, they said.
India's demand for edible oil peaks in the festival months of August, September and October.
"I do not expect any rise in prices despite the festivals becuse of good imports," Shah said.
